interactions.summary: The coinage attempt peters out as Rebecca supplies a word for 'into' and the interviewer laughs that the assembled term still does not work.
Jiang explains that he brought Rebecca in so the interview can hear a student's perspective on why empathy matters in the school and how the school tries to cultivate it.
The interviewer asks Rebecca directly what she has learned about empathy at the school.
Rebecca says a Botswana trip during winter vacation disrupted student stereotypes about Africa and set up an empathy lesson through travel and service learning.
Jiang interrupts to ask Rebecca what specifically in the service-learning experience cultivated empathy.

Rebecca says the trip exposed the empathy limits of an only-child upbringing, then describes learning perspective-taking both through a homestay girl caring for siblings and through half an hour spent trying to understand a nonverbal child with Down syndrome.

claims.claim: Jiang frames Rebecca as firsthand evidence of how the school tries to educate students into empathy rather than only talking about the concept abstractly.
Rebecca says a Botswana trip taken a month earlier during winter vacation confronted student stereotypes about Africa and revealed a different social reality than they expected.
claims.temporal_scope: Student retrospective about a trip one month before the 2012-03-16 interview.

claims.claim: Rebecca says being an only child left her unaccustomed to constantly thinking about siblings or other dependents, which made her homestay experience in Botswana newly instructive.
claims.temporal_scope: Student self-diagnosis stated on 2012-03-16 about earlier Botswana experiences.

claims.claim: Rebecca says working with a nonverbal girl with Down syndrome forced her to spend an unusually long stretch trying to infer another person's wants and feelings, including realizing the girl was thirsty and getting her water.
claims.temporal_scope: Student report of a service-learning experience described on 2012-03-16.

signature_moments.moment: Rebecca realizes that sibling care trains a constant outward attention she never had to practice as an only child.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I never had that experience where I was just worrying about someone else all the time
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It grounds empathy in family structure and lived habit rather than abstract moral exhortation.

signature_moments.moment: Empathy becomes thirty minutes of patient inference beside a girl who cannot speak and cannot properly grip a pen.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the longest time I spent ... just getting into someone other's head
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's clearest lived example of perspective-taking as disciplined attention rather than sentiment.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Rebecca and Jiang use the term for hands-on educational work in Botswana where students encounter unfamiliar lives and must respond concretely to other people's needs.

chronology_notes.note: The interview moves from conceptual translation to concrete evidence by introducing a Botswana trip from roughly one month before the interview as a recent empathy-forming experience for current students.

uncertainty_notes.note: The ASR around Rebecca's description of the homestay girl's siblings is noisy, but the underlying point about constant sibling care and outward concern is clear.
